findings.title: Google Meet booking without a destination calendar throws TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` gives `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no `?.`, so it throws. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. The other handlers in this PR pass `[]`. This fallback exists for 'Meet selected without a Google Cal', so an event type with Meet and no destination calendar now throws in `EventManager.create` instead of falling back to Cal Video. Fix: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Slug condition inverted when rewriting the spread expressions
findings.body: The base code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. It set `slug` only when team billing is disabled. The new line is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which drops the `!`. With billing enabled, the org is now created with the slug straight away, bypassing the `requestedSlug` flow that line 153 still sets. With billing disabled, the org gets no slug at all. This file has nothing to do with multi-destination calendars. Fix: `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, or revert the hunk.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId
findings.body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept `result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video/meeting references are now saved with no credentialId. `createMeeting` does return `credentialId` (`packages/core/videoClient.ts:78`). Later flows that look up a video reference's credential will lose it. Fix: `credentialId: result.credentialId`.

findings.title: updateLocation drops externalCalendarId and credentialId for calendar references
findings.body: `updateLocation` builds references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Calendar results here come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (`packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-322`), which returns neither field. The old code took them from `evt.destinationCalendar`. After this change, the references written after an edit-location call have `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` undefined. Later updates and cancellations then fall back to 'every credential of this type' and to `primary` on Google. This affects `editLocation.handler.ts`. Fix: return `externalId` and `credentialId` from `updateEvent`, or keep the reference's own values in `updateLocation`.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent can never match
findings.body: The fallback runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then calls `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, which compares against that falsy value. The result is `undefined`, or an entry with an empty externalId. The old fallback was `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now `calendarId` is `undefined` for references saved without `externalCalendarId`, and `events.update` fails or targets the wrong calendar. The same pattern is at line 317 in `deleteEvent`, where it falls to `primary` instead of the destination calendar. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (already computed at line 198) in `updateEvent`, and the equivalent in `deleteEvent`.

findings.title: createEvent ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId
findings.body: The target calendar is now chosen only via `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (lines 375-381) still handles destinations without a `credentialId`, which are legacy rows. It calls `createEvent(c, event)` for them, and the new `externalId` argument is not passed. For those rows no entry matches the credential, so the event goes to `primary` instead of the destination's `externalId`. The old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly. Consider falling back to the destination whose `integration` matches the credential type when no `credentialId` match exists.

findings.title: Recurring-delete block now runs once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch (lines 444-468) deletes every remaining booking's first calendar reference on every user calendar credential. It now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. A booking with N calendar references, which is the point of this PR, repeats the whole sweep N times. Each pass fires N× redundant Google/Office delete calls, which return 404/410 on the repeats. Hoist the recurring branch out of the loop so it runs once. A single `bookingToDelete.references.find` per updated booking also only deletes the first calendar reference; consider iterating all of them.

findings.title: Collective members' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (lines 1063-1067). The push at line 1078 is `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which does nothing on `null`. So other collective hosts' calendars are never booked, and the `EventManager` fallback path runs instead. Initialise to `[]` and push the team calendars. Then `EventManager.create` should treat an empty array as 'no destination' (it already does).

findings.title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite changes behaviour and select
findings.body: The `loadUsers` rewrite is not related to the destination-calendar change. It drops the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` select for dynamic users. The `IsFixedAwareUser` type (line 355) still requires `organization`, and the event-type branch still selects it (line 321). It also turns any error into a 400 or 500 `HttpError`, and throws for an empty `dynamicUserList`. Please revert or split it out, or confirm that nothing reads `user.organization` for dynamic groups.

contracts.action: createAllCalendarEvents iterates all destination calendars and fetches missing credentials from DB
contracts.before_after: Before: one destination, credential from the organizer's list only. After: loop with a DB fallback; the reference now stores result.externalId/result.credentialId.

contracts.failure_mode: If the credential is not found or has no app slug it is silently skipped (no error or log). Video references lose their credentialId (line 170), and updateLocation references lose theirs (line 209).

contracts.before_after: Before: used the destination's externalId. After: find() compares against the same falsy value, so it returns nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: Updates and deletes of references without externalCalendarId go to the wrong calendar or fail.
contracts.failure_mode: events.update called with calendarId undefined; Google rejects, error logged, booking update reported as failed.

summary:
I found two blockers and three smaller bugs in the multi-destination-calendar change. I read the changed code and its callers only; nothing was built or run.

- **Blocker, `EventManager.create`:** `packages/core/EventManager.ts:119` reads `.integration` on a destructured value that is `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty. A Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video. `handleNewBooking` sets `destinationCalendar` to null in that case.
- **Blocker, organization create handler:** `create.handler.ts` inverts the `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition when it sets `slug`. The base code set `slug` only when billing was disabled. This file has nothing to do with calendars.
- **Fix, references lose ids:**
  - Video references lose their `credentialId` (`EventManager.ts:170`).
  - After an edit-location call, calendar references lose `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` (`EventManager.ts:209`), because `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns neither.
- **Fix, Google calendar fallback:** the fallback calendar lookup in the Google `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compares against a falsy value, so it never matches. The old code fell back to the destination's `externalId`.
- **Consider:**
  - The Google `createEvent` change sends legacy destination calendars (no `credentialId`) to the `primary` calendar.
  - The recurring-delete block in `handleCancelBooking` now runs once per calendar reference.
  - Collective hosts' calendars are dropped when `destinationCalendar` is null.
  - The `loadUsers` rewrite in `handleNewBooking` is unrelated to this change and drops the `organization` select for dynamic users.
